title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: All Executive and Non-Executive Directors, officers (Key Management Personnel including the CEO), all direct reports to the CEO, all other employees, and closely related persons of all of the above. General insider trading and confidentiality obligations apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors, all other key management personnel (including the CEO), all direct reports of the CEO, and employees notified that they are Restricted Persons. Subject to Trading Windows, the approval process, and the anti-hedging policy.

tiers.name: closely related persons
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, a child of the person's spouse, other family members who may be expected to influence or be influenced by the person, a company or trust over which the person has influence or control, a trust of which the person is a beneficiary (unless the person exercises no control over it), and any other person over whom the person has investment control or influence.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company

windows.start_anchor: beginning of trading on the first trading day after the half year financial results are released
beginning of trading on the first trading day after the March quarterly statements are released
beginning of trading on the first trading day after the full-year financial results are released
beginning of trading on the first trading day after the September quarterly statements are released

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose a restriction on trading during any period (a Closed Period), including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted Trading Window; the Company Secretary notifies Restricted Persons of Closed Period dates. Confidentiality of the existence of a Closed Period is not addressed.

rules.detail: The Trading Request Form expressly lists 'utilise derivatives and enter a hedging transaction' as a type of dealing requiring notice to the Chair (generally via the Company Secretary) and confirmation of no objection before proceeding, and only within a Trading Window or under an exceptional-circumstances approval.
rules.evidence: utilise derivatives and enter a hedging transaction

rules.detail: Absolute ban on transactions with securities or derivatives in associated products that limit the economic risk of unvested equity-based remuneration entitlements. The policy does not separately address vested but locked securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested securities falls outside the anti-hedging ban (limited to unvested entitlements) and is expressly contemplated as a form of dealing on the Trading Request Form, so it is permitted subject to the standard notice-and-clearance process and Trading Window timing.
rules.evidence: utilise derivatives and enter a hedging transaction

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement over vested securities would fall within the broad 'trading' definition (granting or receiving interests in securities) and the derivatives/hedging category on the Trading Request Form, requiring the standard clearance.
rules.evidence: The term "trading" is used for convenience to refer to any form of dealing including but not only buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of, transferring, or granting or receiving interests in securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.

Lending securities is expressly named as a form of dealing, so it is subject to the standard notice-and-clearance regime; the policy flags that 'particular additional restrictions apply' but does not set them out elsewhere in the document.
rules.evidence: Lending securities is a form of dealing in securities (note, particular additional restrictions apply to lending securities).

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but fall within 'derivatives (or any derivative thereof)' and the broad trading/dealing definition, so they are permitted only via the standard clearance process.
rules.evidence: utilise derivatives and enter a hedging transaction

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements are not expressly prohibited; they are implicitly contemplated as legitimate because the policy excludes a lender's forced sale of securities under such an arrangement from the trading restrictions.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement;

rules.detail: Granting, allowing the grant of, or becoming entitled to a security interest in or over securities is expressly included in the definition of 'trading', so encumbering shares is a dealing requiring the standard notice-and-clearance process; it is not prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: granting or receiving interests in securities may include but is not limited to directly or indirectly granting, allowing the grant of or becoming entitled to a security interest in or over securities.

rules.detail: A loan secured on Company Securities is caught as 'trading' via the security-interest limb of the dealing definition and requires clearance to enter into, but is not banned; enforcement/forced sale by the secured lender is separately excluded from the trading restrictions altogether.
rules.evidence: granting or receiving interests in securities may include but is not limited to directly or indirectly granting, allowing the grant of or becoming entitled to a security interest in or over securities.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or short-term/speculative trading rule is stated anywhere in the policy.

clearance.approver: Chair, generally through the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the trade
clearance.evidence: I confirm that subject to you not gaining any Inside Information, you are authorised to deal in Company Securities for the 5 business days following the approval date of the Managing Director and/or CEO.

clearance.approver: the remaining Directors on the Board
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the trade
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify (through the Trading Request Form) to the Chair, generally through the Company Secretary (in the case of the Chair an application to the remaining Directors on the Board), in advance of any proposed dealing in Company Securities.

exceptions.evidence: transfer of securities in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Relevant Person is a beneficiary, but the Restricted Person has no control or influence over the investment decisions made by the superannuation fund or saving scheme
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution investment plan ("DRP") and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement;

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Closed Period and where the Restricted Person could not reasonably have exercised the options at a time prior to the Closed Period

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade

exceptions.approver: Managing Director/CEO (or the Board, if the applicant is the Managing Director/CEO)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship which means a Restricted Person has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the securities.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director/CEO (or the Board, if the applicant is the Managing Director/CEO)
exceptions.evidence: if the Restricted Person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings to transfer or sell the securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for the Restricted Person to do so

exemption_authority: The Managing Director/CEO (or the Board, if the applicant is the Managing Director/CEO) determines severe financial hardship or court order circumstances; the Chair (or the remaining directors, if the applicant is the Chair) determines other exceptional circumstances warranting trading outside a Trading Window, in its/their sole and absolute discretion.

bespoke_clauses.topic: dealing definition sweeps in derivatives, hedging, security interests and lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: granting or receiving interests in securities may include but is not limited to directly or indirectly granting, allowing the grant of or becoming entitled to a security interest in or over securities. Lending securities is a form of dealing in securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the OTC put/call legs and the grant of security over the collared shares are 'dealing' requiring notice and Company Secretary confirmation like an ordinary share trade, but none of these instruments is separately banned outside the unvested-hedging rule.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are not permitted to enter transactions with securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over already-vested shares falls outside the express anti-hedging ban, so vested holdings are eligible subject only to the general clearance and Trading Window regime.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out names margin lending
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement of the bank's security by force-selling the collared shares is expressly excluded from the Trading Window and approval restrictions, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you are authorised to deal in Company Securities for the 5 business days following the approval date of the Managing Director and/or CEO
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar documentation and execution with the bank must be completed within the 5-business-day clearance window unless a longer period is specified.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons should ensure that any securities trading which is prohibited by this Policy is not undertaken by their ... a company or trust over which the Restricted Person has influence or control (regardless of who is the beneficiary)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the clearance obligation or the anti-hedging ban on unvested entitlements.

summary: A funded collar appears achievable under this policy. The anti-hedging ban in clause 14.1 applies only to unvested equity-based remuneration entitlements, so a collar written over vested, unrestricted Company Securities is not itself an express breach. Because 'trading' is defined broadly to include derivatives, hedging transactions and the grant of a security interest over securities, both the put/call legs and the bank's security over the collared shares are Dealings requiring prior notice to, and confirmation from, the Chair (generally via the Company Secretary) or the Board (for the Chair), to be executed within the 5-business-day clearance window and only inside an open Trading Window or under an exceptional-circumstances approval. A lender's forced sale on enforcement, including under a margin lending arrangement, is expressly excluded from the trading restrictions, so the bank's enforcement rights are not blocked by a Closed Period. The executive must notify the Company Secretary of the completed trade within two business days; no minimum shareholding requirement or specific secured-financing disclosure obligation is addressed.
